partner_context.their_ambition: You run one of the world's most-used public marine networks — abras, water buses, water taxis and ferries — and the Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 commits you to 22.2M marine trips a year, a 158 km network, 79 stations and 35 lines by 2030.
partner_context.their_pressure: Growth and UAE Net Zero 2050 both demand fleet renewal and new high-value lines — without disturbing the heritage abra trade that makes Dubai's water unique.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the premium, zero-emission, software-defined edge of that renewal: fast lines today's fleet can't serve, fully additive to the abra cooperative and aligned to the Marine Plan 2030 targets.

hero.title: Dubai RTA × Navier — a premium, zero-emission layer on the water
hero.subtitle: A foiling tier above today's marine network: new high-value lines toward the Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 targets, a clear decarbonization path, and the heritage abra trade left untouched.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a software-defined, zero-emission foiling tier to Dubai's marine network — quiet, fast and low-wake. It opens premium and feeder lines the current fleet can't serve, helps deliver the Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 targets, and gives RTA a credible decarbonization path under UAE Net Zero 2050, fully additive to the abras and water buses.

why_now: The Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 commits Dubai to nearly doubling marine ridership (14.7M → 22.2M/yr), tripling the network length, and going from 7 to 35 lines — while UAE Net Zero 2050 mandates a renewed, electrified fleet. Foiling is the premium edge of that renewal: faster, near-silent, zero-emission, and far more efficient per passenger-mile. A demo vessel is in Dubai now.

proof_points.claim: RTA has a quantified marine-growth mandate.
proof_points.evidence: Marine Transport Master Plan 2030: marine ridership 14.7M → 22.2M/yr (+51%), network 55 → 158 km, stations 48 → 79, lines 7 → 35.

proof_points.claim: RTA already runs marine transport at scale.
proof_points.evidence: Abra, water bus, water taxi and ferry services across the Creek, Water Canal and Gulf coastline, with new stations like Souk Al Marfa at Dubai Islands.
RTA is rolling out partner-operated autonomous vehicles across Dubai — the same software-defined model Navier brings to the water.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the network model in the Maldives; a demo vessel is in Dubai now.

objections.concern: Will this disrupt the heritage abra trade?
objections.response: No — the foiling tier sits above the heritage trade on premium and feeder lines the abras don't serve. It is purely additive and protects the cooperative.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the long-range hybrid covers the Dubai–Abu Dhabi leg with no offshore charging at all.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe in Dubai's busy, shared waterways?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil zones near abra lanes and berths, automatic speed and wake limits in shared water, and conventional low-speed handling everywhere it isn't cleared to fly.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + long-range hybrid), the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: Network integration, berth access, the Marine Plan 2030 mandate and regulatory cover.
the_ask.next_step: A Marina-and-Creek premium pilot, co-specified with RTA against the Marine Plan 2030 targets.

close.title: A premium water layer that grows with the city.
close.body: Start on the Marina and the Creek, scale across the full Marine Plan 2030 network, then connect the capital — a zero-emission foiling tier that advances Dubai 2040 and Net Zero 2050 while protecting the heritage trade that makes Dubai's water unique.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

levers: Navier is the software-defined, zero-emission foiling upgrade to a marine mode Dubai already runs at massive scale and is committed to expanding. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent, low-wake and far more efficient per passenger-mile than the current displacement fleet — opening premium and feeder corridors the abras and water buses can't serve, while sitting entirely above (and protecting) the heritage abra trade.

Every Master Plan 2030 target — more ridership, more network length, more lines, a renewed and electrified fleet — is exactly what a zero-emission foiling tier delivers. Navier is the premium, fast, near-silent edge of the renewal RTA has already committed to, and it advances Net Zero 2050.
